newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK CAPITAL MKT COMMISSIONER SAYS NOT RESIGNING.
newsitem.headline: GREEK CAPITAL MKT COMMISSIONER SAYS NOT RESIGNING.

text.p: Greece's capital market commission president Stavros Thomadakis told Reuters that market rumours of his resignation over comments made on Wednesday that were blamed for today's bourse slump were unfounded.
"There is no such issue," said Thomadakis when asked whether market talk of his resignation was true. "My comments aimed to protect retail investors."
Thomadakis cautioned investors against rumour-based investment decisions on Wednesday.
"All I wanted to do was to recommend calmness in a climate of enthusiasm," he said. "The mission of the capital market commission is to secure normal market conditions and protect investors."
Asked if National Economy Minister Yannos Papandoniou was aware of the content of his comments beforehand on Wednesday, Thomadakis said that this question should be posed to the minister.
His secretary told Reuters earlier that Papandoniou was fully aware of Thomadakis' comments in advance. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4.
